name: PLFM_RADAR
description: Open-source, low-cost 10.5 GHz PLFM phased array RADAR system
one_liner: Blueprints and code to build your own radar system — the kind used to detect moving objects like cars or drones — for a fraction of what commercial radar hardware costs.
buyer: A university robotics/electronics lab, a drone-detection startup, or a hobbyist hardware engineer who needs radar sensing but can't afford commercial radar modules.
business_use_cases: A university lab builds units from the open design for student research projects instead of buying expensive commercial radar kits.
A small startup building low-cost drone-detection systems for warehouses or farms uses the design as a starting hardware reference.
A hardware maker assembles and sells pre-built, calibrated units to hobbyists and small labs who don't want to source parts and solder it themselves.

money_ideas.idea: Sell pre-assembled, tested radar kits built from the open design to labs and makers who don't want to build from scratch.
Offer paid customization and calibration services for specific use cases like drone detection or traffic monitoring.

steal_this: This weekend's build here is realistically a soldering-iron project, not a software one — the honest move is to pre-order the bill of materials, assemble a few working units, and sell them at a markup to university labs on a specialty electronics marketplace.
